tools.name: repoctl_status
tools.title: Set status
tools.description: Show the package set in the current directory: targets, lock state of each package worktree (in-sync, ahead, behind, dirty), the active run, the last run and the last publish. Call this first in a new session. Returns kind Status.

tools.name: repoctl_doctor
tools.title: Check the build host
tools.description: Check that this host can build the set: mock group membership, mock configs of each target, rpmautospec plugin, GPG key, createrepo_c, disk space, XDG directories, reachability of external git URLs, and that the installed skills match the binary. Each check is ok, warning or failed, with a remediation line. Use it when a build fails before the srpm step. Returns kind DoctorReport.

tools.name: repoctl_show
tools.title: Show packages
tools.description: Show packages of the set: source branch or external URL, locked commit, worktree HEAD and state, targets, version and release per target, upstream settings and the notes from repoctl.yaml. Read the notes before you propose a version change: they hold rules such as 'upstream 4.x is frozen'. Returns kind Package, one item per dir. Maps to repoctl list (all) and repoctl show <dir>.

dirs.description: Package dirs, e.g. ["ucx"]. Empty or absent: all packages.

tools.name: repoctl_graph
tools.title: Build graph
tools.description: Return the dependency graph of each target. An edge from A to B means A must be built before B; via lists the BuildRequires that matched. unresolved lists requires that only a node of another target provides: these often cause a builddep failure. Returns kind Graph, one item per target.

targets.description: Target ids, e.g. ["el10"]. Absent: all targets.

tools.name: repoctl_plan
tools.title: Plan a build
tools.description: Show what a build would do and why, without building. Each node gets action build, cached or skip. A build node lists reasons with a code: commit-changed, dep-key-changed, macros-changed, mock-config-changed, not-in-cache or forced. Read warnings: nvr.reused means the rebuilt package keeps its published NVR (publish will refuse it; repoctl bump-release fixes it), and dep.not-for-target predicts a builddep failure. The first plan of a target can take minutes because repoctl builds SRPMs to read their requires. Returns kind Plan.

dirs.description: Limit to these package dirs and their dependents. Absent: all.

force.description: Plan the selected nodes as build even if cached (reason forced).

tools.name: repoctl_upstream
tools.title: Upstream versions
tools.description: Compare each package version with the latest upstream release (GitHub tags or releases with the tag filter from repoctl.yaml, and the Fedora rawhide version). status is up-to-date, update-available, ahead or unknown. newer lists the tags between the current and the latest version; use releaseNotesUrl to read what changed. Answers are cached for one hour unless refresh is true. Returns kind Upstream.

tools.name: repoctl_runs
tools.title: Run history
tools.description: List recent build and publish runs of the set, newest first, with state and node counts. Use it to find the run id of the last failed build. Returns kind Run with nodes left empty; call repoctl_run_get for the nodes.

tools.name: repoctl_run_get
tools.title: Run details
tools.description: Return one run with every node: state (queued, waiting, running, ok, cached, failed, blocked, canceled), steps with durations and exit codes, NVRs, artifacts, log paths, and for a failed node an error with class and a log excerpt. Works while the run is in progress. publishable lists targets a person may publish; publishBlockers says why the others are not. next lists suggested steps; a step with human: true is for the person only. Returns kind Run.

artifacts.description: Include the artifact list of each node (file, path, size, sha256). Absent: NVRs only.

tools.name: repoctl_run_wait
tools.title: Wait for a run
tools.description: Wait until a run ends or timeoutSeconds pass, then return the run as repoctl_run_get does. Sends MCP progress notifications (nodes ended of nodes planned) when the call has a progressToken. If the run is not done when the time ends, call the tool again. Do not poll faster: one call can wait up to 600 seconds.

artifacts.description: Include the artifact list of each node (file, path, size, sha256). Absent: NVRs only.

tools.name: repoctl_logs
tools.title: Node log
tools.description: Return lines (repoctl logs RUN NODE) of the log of one node in a run (all steps: srpm, rpm, stage, with mock root.log and build.log merged in). By default it returns the error excerpt and the last 120 lines. Use grep to find a pattern such as 'error:' or 'Failed build dependencies'. Returns kind NodeLog; lines are escaped and each line is cut at 2000 bytes.

run.description: Run id. Absent: the newest run that has this node.

grep.description: RE2 regular expression; returns matching lines with 3 lines of context, at most 400 lines.

tools.name: repoctl_repo_ls
tools.title: Repo contents
tools.description: List the RPMs in the published repos, or in the staging repo of a run. One item per target and repo (slurm, slurm-source, slurm-debuginfo). Returns kind RepoContents.

run.description: Staging repo of this run. Absent: published repos.

name.description: Glob on the package name, e.g. slurm-*.

tools.name: repoctl_repo_diff
tools.title: Staging vs published
tools.description: Compare the staging repo of a run with the published repo: added, removed, changed (other EVR) and rebuilt (same NVRA, other payload). Use it to write the summary a person reads before they publish. Returns kind RepoDiff, one item per target and repo.

tools.name: repoctl_build
tools.title: Build to staging
tools.description: Start a build of the set into a new staging repo and return when the plan is ready, with the run id. It never signs and never publishes. It never builds uncommitted files: a dirty worktree fails with code lock.dirty and a humanAction. With from=lock (default), every selected worktree must match repoctl.lock (else lock.dirty). Only one run per set: an active run gives code set.busy and its id; wait for it with repoctl_run_wait. Follow the new run with repoctl_run_wait. Returns kind Run (state planning or running).

dirs.description: Build these packages and their dependents. Absent: all.

from.description: lock: pinned commits (publishable). worktree: worktree HEAD commits, to try a commit before pin; the run is never publishable.

failFast.description: Stop after the first failure. Default: keep going with independent nodes.

rdeps.description: Also build the packages that depend on dirs.

tools.name: repoctl_run_cancel
tools.title: Cancel a run
tools.description: Cancel a build run that this MCP server started (repoctl cancel). Running nodes are stopped, queued and waiting nodes end canceled, the staging repo keeps the nodes that ended ok. A run started from the CLI or the web UI is not canceled: the call fails with code cancel.foreign-run and a humanAction.

tools.name: repoctl_pin
tools.title: Pin worktree commits
tools.description: Write the HEAD commit of the named package worktrees into repoctl.lock. Use it after you commit a spec change in packages/<dir>. It does not commit repoctl.lock and does not push. It refuses a dirty worktree (code lock.dirty, with a humanAction). Returns kind Lock with previous and new commits.

tools.name: repoctl_checkout
tools.title: Check out locked commits
tools.description: Create or update package worktrees at the commits in repoctl.lock, and fetch external mirrors. It never discards changes: a dirty worktree or a worktree with commits that are not in the lock fails with code lock.dirty and a humanAction. Returns kind Lock.
